## Objective
- Complete and validate the browser-based pixel RPG, including usable gear, bike travel, and Kanto towns with distinct services and content.
- Replace destination-button travel with Pokémon-style world traversal: the player moves a character through the world using a gamepad.

## Requirements
- Include battles, recruitment, Kanto towns and gyms, upgrades, rivals, localStorage saves, playable slots and prizes, daycare, fusion, fighting club, and Boss-rank organization management.
- All 151 Pokémon must be breedable and fusable; captured/generated creatures must be battle-ready.
- Elite Four requires eight badges and three Victory Road stages; each Elite Four trainer has six high-level Pokémon.
- Safari Zone opens at Grunt rank with captures and business income; random map trainers can be battled and stolen from.
- Pokémon equipment: one Pokémon-specific item per creature; player slots: hat, shirt, pants, gloves, shoes, and two accessories.
- Bike use must be available outdoors and in caves, but not inside buildings, with a meaningful travel benefit.
- Towns should feature source-inspired services, including healing centers and Pokémarts.
- Inspect a JPEG screenshot at viewport width ≤1280px and briefly note reasonable assumptions.

## Decisions
- Use a self-contained HTML/CSS/JavaScript game with localStorage key `neon-syndicate-save`.
- Switching creatures uses the player’s turn; a healthy teammate automatically takes over when one faints.
- Breeding selects two parents and a species from the 151-Pokémon catalog; fusion consumes two creatures, adds generation-based stats, and can be repeated.
- Rival is Nia Vale; the story includes stealing her bike.
- Use Generation I type assignments and interactions; player gear bonuses are attack, defense, and max HP.
- Existing bike theft event says Kanto travel becomes free, but travel must now be character-driven rather than destination-button travel.

## Work State

### Completed
- Implemented game shell, campaign progression, battles, recruitment, upgrades, slots and prizes, daycare, fighting club, breeding, repeatable fusion, organization controls, and save migration (`leagueVersion:2`).
- Added 151-species catalog, eight Gym stages, three Victory Road stages, six-creature Elite Four parties and champion party.
- Added Kanto destinations, Gym panels, League and Safari panels, bike-theft state, Safari captures/business, and random local trainer interactions.
- Added gear definitions, seven player slots, Pokémon equipment mapping, inventory, and save normalization/migration.

### Active
- Change field travel to a Pokémon-style world where a gamepad moves the character; support outdoor and cave bike use, disallow bike indoors, and make it meaningfully faster.
- Add town-specific service/content panels, including healing centers and Pokémarts, with functioning actions and credit costs.
- Build equipment shopping, inventory, and equip UI; apply player and Pokémon gear bonuses in combat.
- Run `/tmp/opencode/validate-game.mjs`, test gameplay/save migration, and inspect/update `screenshots/neon-syndicate.jpg` at ≤1280px.

### Blocked
- (none)

## Next Move
1. Inspect the existing map rendering and input code in `game.js`; add a traversable world with character movement by gamepad, plus keyboard fallback if appropriate.
2. Connect locations, buildings, and caves to world interactions; ensure bike restrictions and travel benefits work.
3. Continue town services and gear UI/combat integration.
4. Run `/tmp/opencode/validate-game.mjs`, test gameplay and save migration, and inspect/update the JPEG screenshot.

## Relevant Files
- `game.js`: Game logic, field/map rendering, travel, bike event, town rendering, gear data, save migration, and combat.
- `index.html`: Game shell and interactive UI roots.
- `style.css`: Layout and responsive styling.
- `/tmp/opencode/validate-game.mjs`: Playwright validation script.
- `screenshots/neon-syndicate.jpg`: Existing screenshot to inspect/update.

- Current field destinations are clicked through `[data-travel]` controls in `renderField()`; their click handler directly changes `state.location`.

- Changes are uncommitted; project files are untracked.

## Objective
- Complete the browser-based pixel RPG with Pokémon-style character movement instead of destination-button travel.
- Finish remaining gameplay systems, including TM/HM learning, then validate gameplay, saves, and the responsive screenshot.

## Requirements
- Include battles, recruitment, Kanto towns and Gyms, upgrades, rivals, localStorage saves, playable slots and prizes, daycare, fusion, fighting club, and Boss-rank organization management.
- Make all 151 Pokémon breedable and fusable; generated creatures must be battle-ready.
- Require eight badges and three Victory Road stages for the Elite Four; each Elite Four trainer has six high-level Pokémon.
- Open Safari Zone at Grunt rank with captures and business income; allow battles and theft from random map trainers.
- Support one Pokémon-specific item per creature and player gear slots for hat, shirt, pants, gloves, shoes, and two accessories.
- Make bike travel available outdoors and in caves, unavailable inside buildings, and meaningfully faster.
- Give towns distinct, functioning services, including healing centers and Pokémarts.
- Pokémon must be able to learn TMs and HMs.
- Validate gameplay and save migration; inspect a JPEG screenshot at viewport width ≤1280px and briefly note reasonable assumptions.

## Decisions
- Use a self-contained HTML/CSS/JavaScript game with localStorage key `neon-syndicate-save`.
- Switching creatures uses the player’s turn; a healthy teammate automatically takes over when one faints.
- Breeding selects two parents and a species from the 151-Pokémon catalog; fusion consumes two creatures, adds generation-based stats, and can be repeated.
- Rival is Nia Vale; the story includes stealing her bike.
- Use Generation I type assignments and interactions; player gear bonuses are attack, defense, and max HP.
- Existing bike theft event says Kanto travel becomes free, but travel must be character-driven rather than destination-button travel.

## Work State
### Completed
- Implemented game shell, campaign progression, battles, recruitment, upgrades, slots and prizes, daycare, fighting club, breeding, repeatable fusion, organization controls, and save migration (`leagueVersion:2`).
- Added 151-species catalog, eight Gym stages, three Victory Road stages, six-creature Elite Four parties and champion party.
- Added Kanto destinations, Gym panels, League and Safari panels, bike-theft state, Safari captures/business, and random local trainer interactions.
- Added gear definitions, seven player slots, Pokémon equipment mapping, inventory, and save normalization/migration.

### Active
- Implement Pokémon-style traversable world movement with gamepad controls; current field travel still uses clickable `[data-travel]` destination buttons and `drawMap()` is static.
- Add learnable TMs and HMs to Pokémon, persist learned moves, and make them usable in battle.
- Connect world locations and indoor/cave transitions; enforce bike restrictions and travel speed.
- Add town-specific service panels and functioning actions, including healing centers and Pokémarts.
- Build equipment shopping, inventory, and equip UI; apply player and Pokémon gear bonuses in combat.
- Run `/tmp/opencode/validate-game.mjs`, test gameplay/save migration, and inspect/update `screenshots/neon-syndicate.jpg` at ≤1280px.

### Blocked
- (none)

## Next Move
1. Inspect remaining `game.js` input handlers and map rendering, then implement continuous character movement with gamepad and keyboard fallback.
2. Implement TM/HM learning and connect learned moves to battle actions.
3. Connect locations, buildings, and caves to world interactions; enforce bike restrictions and faster travel.
4. Finish town services and gear UI/combat integration.
5. Run validation, test gameplay/save migration, and inspect/update the JPEG screenshot.

## Relevant Files
- `game.js`: Game logic, field/map rendering and travel, town panels, bike state, gear, save migration, and combat.
- `index.html`: Game shell and interactive UI roots.
- `style.css`: Layout and responsive styling.
- `/tmp/opencode/validate-game.mjs`: Playwright validation script.
- `screenshots/neon-syndicate.jpg`: Existing screenshot to inspect/update.

## Important Context
- Current field destinations are clicked through `[data-travel]` controls in `renderField()`; their click handler directly changes `state.location`.
- `drawMap()` renders a static canvas; `drawBase()` draws a character sprite but does not establish field traversal.
- `stealNiasBike()` sets `state.bikeStolen=true` and reports “Kanto travel is now free.”
- `INITIAL` includes `insideBuilding`, `bikeMode`, `world:{x:360,y:285}`, and `potions:0`; these fields are not yet wired into behavior or save migration.
- No changes were made in the latest turn; files remain uncommitted.

messages.summary:
## Objective
- Complete the browser-based pixel RPG with Pokémon-style movement and remaining gameplay systems, especially TM/HM learning.
- Validate gameplay, save migration, and a responsive screenshot.

## Requirements
- Include battles, recruitment, Kanto towns and Gyms, upgrades, rivals, localStorage saves, playable slots and prizes, daycare, fusion, fighting club, and Boss-rank organization management.
- Make all 151 Pokémon breedable and fusable; generated creatures must be battle-ready.
- Require eight badges and three Victory Road stages for the Elite Four; each Elite Four trainer has six high-level Pokémon.
- Open Safari Zone at Grunt rank with captures and business income; allow battles and theft from random map trainers.
- Support one Pokémon-specific item per creature and player gear slots for hat, shirt, pants, gloves, shoes, and two accessories.
- Make bike travel available outdoors and in caves, unavailable inside buildings, and meaningfully faster.
- Give towns distinct, functioning services, including healing centers and Pokémarts.
- TMs should be single-use and reobtainable.
- HMs should be found once, then reusable to teach eligible Pokémon repeatedly.

## Decisions
- Use a self-contained HTML/CSS/JavaScript game with localStorage key `neon-syndicate-save`.
- Switching creatures uses the player’s turn; a healthy teammate automatically takes over when one faints.
- Breeding selects two parents and a species from the 151-Pokémon catalog; fusion consumes two creatures, adds generation-based stats, and can be repeated.
- Rival is Nia Vale; the story includes stealing her bike.
- Use Generation I type assignments and interactions; player gear bonuses are attack, defense, and max HP.
- Existing bike theft event says Kanto travel becomes free, but travel must be character-driven rather than destination-button travel.

## Work State
### Completed
- Implemented game shell, campaign progression, battles, recruitment, upgrades, slots and prizes, daycare, fighting club, breeding, repeatable fusion, organization controls, and save migration (`leagueVersion:2`).
- Added 151-species catalog, eight Gym stages, three Victory Road stages, six-creature Elite Four parties and champion party.
- Added Kanto destinations, Gym panels, League and Safari panels, bike-theft state, Safari captures/business, and random local trainer interactions.
- Added gear definitions, seven player slots, Pokémon equipment mapping, inventory, and save normalization/migration.

### Active
- Replace clickable `[data-travel]` destination buttons and static `drawMap()` with traversable character movement and gamepad/keyboard controls.
- Implement persistent learned moves and TM/HM items: TMs consumed on use and reobtainable; HMs found once and reusable for teaching eligible Pokémon repeatedly. Connect moves to battle.
- Connect locations, buildings, and caves to world interactions; enforce bike restrictions and faster travel.
- Finish functioning town services and gear shopping, inventory/equip UI, and combat bonuses.
- Run `/tmp/opencode/validate-game.mjs`, test gameplay and save migration, and inspect/update `screenshots/neon-syndicate.jpg` at viewport width ≤1280px.

### Blocked
- (none)

## Next Move
1. Inspect remaining movement and map-rendering code; implement continuous character movement with gamepad and keyboard fallback.
2. Add learned moves and reusable HM / single-use TM item behavior, eligibility checks, and battle actions.
3. Connect locations, buildings, travel restrictions, and bike speed to world interactions.
4. Finish town services and gear UI/combat integration.
5. Run validation, test gameplay/save migration, and inspect the screenshot.

## Relevant Files
- `game.js`: Game logic, field/map rendering and travel, town panels, bike state, gear, save migration, and combat.
- `index.html`: Game shell and interactive UI roots.
- `style.css`: Layout and responsive styling.
- `/tmp/opencode/validate-game.mjs`: Playwright validation script.
- `screenshots/neon-syndicate.jpg`: Existing screenshot to inspect/update.

## Important Context
- Current field destinations are clicked through `[data-travel]` controls in `renderField()`; their click handler directly changes `state.location`.
- `drawMap()` renders a static canvas; `drawBase()` draws a character sprite but does not establish field traversal.
- `stealNiasBike()` sets `state.bikeStolen=true` and reports “Kanto travel is now free.”
- `INITIAL` includes `insideBuilding`, `bikeMode`, `world:{x:360,y:285}`, and `potions:0`; these fields are not yet wired into behavior or save migration.
- `fieldTrainer()` persists random trainer encounters by location; `startMapTrainer()` starts their battles.
- Repository changes are uncommitted; `git status --short` showed untracked `.gitignore`, `Agents.md`, `capture.sh`, `game.js`, `index.html`, `start.sh`, `startup.sh`, and `style.css`.

## Objective

- Include battles, recruitment, Kanto towns and Gyms, upgrades, rivals, localStorage saves, playable slots and prizes, daycare, fusion, fighting club, and Boss-rank organization management.
- Make all 151 Pokémon breedable and fusable; generated creatures must be battle-ready.
- Require eight badges and three Victory Road stages for the Elite Four; each Elite Four trainer has six high-level Pokémon.
- Open Safari Zone at Grunt rank with captures and business income; allow battles and theft from random map trainers.
- Support one Pokémon-specific item per creature and player gear slots for hat, shirt, pants, gloves, shoes, and two accessories.
- Make bike travel available outdoors and in caves, unavailable inside buildings, and meaningfully faster.
- Give towns distinct, functioning services, including healing centers and Pokémarts.
- TMs should be single-use and reobtainable; HMs should be found once and teach eligible Pokémon repeatedly.
- Use character-driven travel rather than destination-button travel.

## Decisions
- Use a self-contained HTML/CSS/JavaScript game with localStorage key `neon-syndicate-save`.
- Switching creatures uses the player’s turn; a healthy teammate automatically takes over when one faints.
- Breeding selects two parents and a species from the 151-Pokémon catalog; fusion consumes two creatures, adds generation-based stats, and can be repeated.
- Rival is Nia Vale; the story includes stealing her bike.
- Use Generation I type assignments and interactions; player gear bonuses are attack, defense, and max HP.
- Existing bike theft event says Kanto travel becomes free, but travel must be character-driven rather than destination-button travel.

### Completed
- Implemented game shell, campaign progression, battles, recruitment, upgrades, slots and prizes, daycare, fighting club, breeding, repeatable fusion, organization controls, and save migration (`leagueVersion:2`).
- Added 151-species catalog, eight Gym stages, three Victory Road stages, six-creature Elite Four parties and champion party.
- Added Kanto destinations, Gym panels, League and Safari panels, bike-theft state, Safari captures/business, and random local trainer interactions.
- Added gear definitions, seven player slots, Pokémon equipment mapping, inventory, and save normalization/migration.

### Active
- Replace clickable `[data-travel]` destination buttons and static `drawMap()` with traversable character movement and gamepad/keyboard controls.
- Implement persistent learned moves and reusable HM / single-use TM item behavior, eligibility checks, and battle actions.
- Connect locations, buildings, and caves to world interactions; enforce bike restrictions and faster travel.
- Finish functioning town services and gear shopping, inventory/equip UI, and combat bonuses.

messages.summary:
## Objective
- Complete the browser-based pixel RPG with Pokémon-style movement and remaining gameplay systems, especially TM/HM learning.
- Validate gameplay, save migration, and a responsive screenshot.

## Requirements
- Include battles, recruitment, Kanto towns and Gyms, upgrades, rivals, localStorage saves, playable slots and prizes, daycare, fusion, fighting club, and Boss-rank organization management.
- Make all 151 Pokémon breedable and fusable; generated creatures must be battle-ready.
- Require eight badges and three Victory Road stages for the Elite Four; each Elite Four trainer has six high-level Pokémon.
- Open Safari Zone at Grunt rank with captures and business income; allow battles and theft from random map trainers.
- Support one Pokémon-specific item per creature and player gear slots for hat, shirt, pants, gloves, shoes, and two accessories.
- Make bike travel available outdoors and in caves, unavailable inside buildings, and meaningfully faster.
- Give towns distinct, functioning services, including healing centers and Pokémarts.
- TMs should be single-use and reobtainable; HMs should be found once and teach eligible Pokémon repeatedly.
- Use character-driven travel rather than destination-button travel.

## Decisions
- Use a self-contained HTML/CSS/JavaScript game with localStorage key `neon-syndicate-save`.
- Switching creatures uses the player’s turn; a healthy teammate automatically takes over when one faints.
- Breeding selects two parents and a species from the 151-Pokémon catalog; fusion consumes two creatures, adds generation-based stats, and can be repeated.
- Rival is Nia Vale; the story includes stealing her bike.
- Use Generation I type assignments and interactions; player gear bonuses are attack, defense, and max HP.
- Existing bike theft event says Kanto travel becomes free, but travel must be character-driven rather than destination-button travel.

## Work State
### Completed
- Implemented game shell, campaign progression, battles, recruitment, upgrades, slots and prizes, daycare, fighting club, breeding, repeatable fusion, organization controls, and save migration (`leagueVersion:2`).
- Added 151-species catalog, eight Gym stages, three Victory Road stages, six-creature Elite Four parties and champion party.
- Added Kanto destinations, Gym panels, League and Safari panels, bike-theft state, Safari captures/business, and random local trainer interactions.
- Added gear definitions, seven player slots, Pokémon equipment mapping, inventory, and save normalization/migration.

### Active
- Replace clickable `[data-travel]` destination buttons and static `drawMap()` with traversable character movement and gamepad/keyboard controls.
- Implement persistent learned moves and reusable HM / single-use TM item behavior, eligibility checks, and battle actions.
- Connect locations, buildings, and caves to world interactions; enforce bike restrictions and faster travel.
- Finish functioning town services and gear shopping, inventory/equip UI, and combat bonuses.
- Run `/tmp/opencode/validate-game.mjs`, test gameplay and save migration, and inspect/update `screenshots/neon-syndicate.jpg` at viewport width ≤1280px.

### Blocked
- (none)

## Next Move
1. Inspect remaining movement and map-rendering code; implement continuous character movement with gamepad and keyboard fallback.
2. Add learned moves and reusable HM / single-use TM item behavior, eligibility checks, and battle actions.
3. Connect locations, buildings, travel restrictions, and bike speed to world interactions.
4. Finish town services and gear UI/combat integration.
5. Run validation, test gameplay/save migration, and inspect the screenshot.

## Relevant Files
- `game.js`: Game logic, field/map rendering and travel, town panels, bike state, gear, save migration, and combat.
- `index.html`: Game shell and interactive UI roots.
- `style.css`: Layout and responsive styling.
- `/tmp/opencode/validate-game.mjs`: Playwright validation script.
- `screenshots/neon-syndicate.jpg`: Existing screenshot to inspect/update.

## Important Context
- Current field destinations are clicked through `[data-travel]` controls in `renderField()`; their click handler directly changes `state.location`.
- `drawMap()` renders a static canvas; `drawBase()` draws a character sprite but does not establish field traversal.
- `stealNiasBike()` sets `state.bikeStolen=true` and reports “Kanto travel is now free.”
- `INITIAL` includes `insideBuilding`, `bikeMode`, `world:{x:360,y:285}`, and `potions:0`; these fields are not yet wired into behavior or save migration.
- `fieldTrainer()` persists random trainer encounters by location; `startMapTrainer()` starts their battles.
- Repository changes are uncommitted; `git status --short` showed untracked `.gitignore`, `Agents.md`, `capture.sh`, `game.js`, `index.html`, `start.sh`, `startup.sh`, and `style.css`.

messages.summary:
## Objective
- Complete the browser-based pixel RPG with Pokémon-style movement and remaining gameplay systems, especially TM/HM learning.
- Validate gameplay, save migration, and a responsive screenshot.

## Requirements
- Include battles, recruitment, Kanto towns and Gyms, upgrades, rivals, localStorage saves, playable slots and prizes, daycare, fusion, fighting club, and Boss-rank organization management.
- Make all 151 Pokémon breedable and fusable; generated creatures must be battle-ready.
- Require eight badges and three Victory Road stages for the Elite Four; each Elite Four trainer has six high-level Pokémon.
- Open Safari Zone at Grunt rank with captures and business income; allow battles and theft from random map trainers.
- Support one Pokémon-specific item per creature and player gear slots for hat, shirt, pants, gloves, shoes, and two accessories.
- Make bike travel available outdoors and in caves, unavailable inside buildings, and meaningfully faster.
- Give towns distinct, functioning services, including healing centers and Pokémarts.
- TMs should be single-use and reobtainable; HMs should be found once and teach eligible Pokémon repeatedly.
- Use character-driven travel rather than destination-button travel.

## Decisions
- Use a self-contained HTML/CSS/JavaScript game with localStorage key `neon-syndicate-save`.
- Switching creatures uses the player’s turn; a healthy teammate automatically takes over when one faints.
- Breeding selects two parents and a species from the 151-Pokémon catalog; fusion consumes two creatures, adds generation-based stats, and can be repeated.
- Rival is Nia Vale; the story includes stealing her bike.
- Use Generation I type assignments and interactions; player gear bonuses are attack, defense, and max HP.
- Existing bike theft event says Kanto travel becomes free, but travel must be character-driven rather than destination-button travel.

## Work State
### Completed
- Implemented game shell, campaign progression, battles, recruitment, upgrades, slots and prizes, daycare, fighting club, breeding, repeatable fusion, organization controls, and save migration (`leagueVersion:2`).
- Added 151-species catalog, eight Gym stages, three Victory Road stages, six-creature Elite Four parties and champion party.
- Added Kanto destinations, Gym panels, League and Safari panels, bike-theft state, Safari captures/business, and random local trainer interactions.
- Added gear definitions, seven player slots, Pokémon equipment mapping, inventory, and save normalization/migration.

### Active
- Replace clickable `[data-travel]` destination buttons and static `drawMap()` with traversable character movement and gamepad/keyboard controls.
- Add persistent learned moves and reusable HM / single-use TM item behavior, eligibility checks, and battle actions.
- Connect locations, buildings, and caves to world interactions; enforce bike restrictions and faster travel.
- Finish functioning town services and gear shopping, inventory/equip UI, and combat bonuses.
- Run validation, test gameplay/save migration, and inspect/update `screenshots/neon-syndicate.jpg` at viewport width ≤1280px.

### Blocked
- (none)

## Next Move
1. Implement continuous character movement using keyboard and gamepad, replacing destination buttons with map-based travel.
2. Add learned moves, TM/HM inventory and use rules, eligibility checks, and battle actions.
3. Connect buildings, caves, travel restrictions, bike speed, town services, gear shopping/equipment, and combat bonuses.
4. Run `/tmp/opencode/validate-game.mjs`, verify gameplay and save migration, and inspect/update the screenshot.

## Relevant Files
- `game.js`: Game logic, field/map rendering and travel, town panels, bike state, gear, save migration, and combat.
- `index.html`: Game shell and interactive UI roots.
- `style.css`: Layout and responsive styling.
- `/tmp/opencode/validate-game.mjs`: Playwright validation script.
- `screenshots/neon-syndicate.jpg`: Existing screenshot to inspect/update.

## Important Context
- `renderField()` currently renders a destination board with `[data-travel]` buttons; its handler directly changes `state.location`.
- `drawMap()` draws a static canvas; `drawBase()` draws a character sprite but does not enable traversal.
- `INITIAL` includes `insideBuilding`, `bikeMode`, `world:{x:360,y:285}`, and `potions:0`; these are not yet wired into behavior or save migration.
- `fieldTrainer()` persists random trainer encounters by location; `startMapTrainer()` starts their battles.
- `game.js` is 293 lines (about 71 KB); validation currently expects `[data-travel="Cerulean City"]` and will need updating for movement-based travel.
- Repository changes are uncommitted; `git status --short` showed untracked `.gitignore`, `Agents.md`, `capture.sh`, `game.js`, `index.html`, `start.sh`, `startup.sh`, and `style.css`.

messages.summary:
## Objective
- Complete the browser-based pixel RPG’s gameplay systems, especially character-driven travel and usable TM/HMs.
- Ensure Gym victories award clearly named badges and include all source-material TMs and HMs.

## Requirements
- Include battles, recruitment, Kanto towns and Gyms, upgrades, rivals, localStorage saves, playable slots and prizes, daycare, fusion, fighting club, and Boss-rank organization management.
- Make all 151 Pokémon breedable and fusable; generated creatures must be battle-ready.
- Require eight badges and three Victory Road stages for the Elite Four; each Elite Four trainer has six high-level Pokémon.
- Open Safari Zone at Grunt rank with captures and business income; allow battles and theft from random map trainers.
- Support one Pokémon-specific item per creature and player gear slots for hat, shirt, pants, gloves, shoes, and two accessories.
- Make bike travel available outdoors and in caves, unavailable inside buildings, and meaningfully faster.
- Give towns distinct, functioning services, including healing centers and Pokémarts.
- TMs should be single-use and reobtainable; HMs should be found once and teach eligible Pokémon repeatedly.
- HMs retain their travel abilities and do not require badges to use.
- Use character-driven travel rather than destination-button travel.
- Gym victories should award badges.
- Include all TMs and HMs from source material.

## Decisions
- Use a self-contained HTML/CSS/JavaScript game with localStorage key `neon-syndicate-save`.
- Switching creatures uses the player’s turn; a healthy teammate automatically takes over when one faints.
- Breeding selects two parents and a species from the 151-Pokémon catalog; fusion consumes two creatures, adds generation-based stats, and can be repeated.
- Rival is Nia Vale; the story includes stealing her bike.
- Use Generation I type assignments and interactions; player gear bonuses are attack, defense, and max HP.
- Existing bike theft event says Kanto travel becomes free, but travel must be character-driven rather than destination-button travel.

## Work State
### Completed
- Implemented game shell, campaign progression, battles, recruitment, upgrades, slots and prizes, daycare, fighting club, breeding, repeatable fusion, organization controls, and save migration (`leagueVersion:2`).
- Added 151-species catalog, eight Gym stages, three Victory Road stages, six-creature Elite Four parties and champion party.
- Added badge names (Boulder, Cascade, Thunder, Rainbow, Soul, Marsh, Volcano, Earth); Gym victories now explicitly announce earning the badge and badge progress lists earned badge names.
- Expanded `MOVE_ITEMS` data in `game.js` from four HMs and three TMs to all 50 Generation I TMs and five HMs, with move names, types, source power, eligibility approximation, and HM travel metadata.

### Active
- Replace clickable `[data-travel]` destination buttons and static `drawMap()` with traversable character movement and keyboard/gamepad controls.
- Implement TM/HM inventory, eligibility checks, Pokémon learning, persistent saves, travel actions, and battle moves; HMs must be reusable and usable for travel without badge gates, while TMs are single-use and reobtainable.
- Connect locations, buildings, and caves to world interactions; enforce bike restrictions and faster travel.
- Finish functioning town services and gear shopping, inventory/equip UI, and combat bonuses.
- Update validation for movement-based travel; run `/tmp/opencode/validate-game.mjs`, test gameplay and save migration, and inspect/update `screenshots/neon-syndicate.jpg` at viewport width ≤1280px.

### Blocked
- (none)

## Next Move
1. Wire the expanded TM/HM catalog to shops or item discovery, Pokémon learning, persistent saves, travel actions, and battle moves.
2. Implement continuous character movement, replacing destination buttons; connect buildings/caves, town services, and bike behavior.
3. Finish gear/inventory/equipment and combat bonuses.
4. Update and run validation, test save migration, and inspect/update the screenshot.

## Relevant Files
- `game.js`: Game logic, Gym badges, map/travel, move-machine catalog, town panels, saves, and combat.
- `index.html`: Game shell and interactive UI roots.
- `style.css`: Layout and responsive styling.
- `/tmp/opencode/validate-game.mjs`: Playwright validation script.
- `screenshots/neon-syndicate.jpg`: Existing screenshot to inspect/update.

## Important Context
- Repository changes are uncommitted.
- `MACHINE_CATALOG` now contains TM01–TM50; `HM_CATALOG` contains HM01–HM05. `MOVE_ITEMS` is derived from these catalogs; learning, inventory, battle, and travel behavior remain unimplemented.
- `renderField()` still renders a destination board with `[data-travel]` buttons; its handler directly changes `state.location`.
- `drawMap()` draws a static canvas; `drawBase()` draws a character sprite but does not enable traversal.
- `INITIAL` includes `insideBuilding`, `bikeMode`, `world:{x:360,y:285}`, and `potions:0`; these are not yet wired into behavior or save migration.
- `/tmp/opencode/validate-game.mjs` currently expects `[data-travel="Cerulean City"]` and must be revised for character-driven travel.

messages.summary:
## Objective
- Complete the browser-based pixel RPG’s gameplay systems, especially character-driven travel and usable TM/HMs.
- Ensure Gym victories award clearly named badges and include all source-material TMs and HMs.

## Requirements
- Include battles, recruitment, Kanto towns and Gyms, upgrades, rivals, localStorage saves, playable slots and prizes, daycare, fusion, fighting club, and Boss-rank organization management.
- Make all 151 Pokémon breedable and fusable; generated creatures must be battle-ready.
- Require eight badges and three Victory Road stages for the Elite Four; each Elite Four trainer has six high-level Pokémon.
- Open Safari Zone at Grunt rank with captures and business income; allow battles and theft from random map trainers.
- Support one Pokémon-specific item per creature and player gear slots for hat, shirt, pants, gloves, shoes, and two accessories.
- Make bike travel available outdoors and in caves, unavailable inside buildings, and meaningfully faster.
- Give towns distinct, functioning services, including healing centers and Pokémarts.
- TMs should be single-use and reobtainable; HMs should be found once and teach eligible Pokémon repeatedly.
- HMs retain their travel abilities and do not require badges to use.
- Use character-driven travel rather than destination-button travel.
- Gym victories should award badges.
- Include all TMs and HMs from source material.

## Decisions
- Use a self-contained HTML/CSS/JavaScript game with localStorage key `neon-syndicate-save`.
- Switching creatures uses the player’s turn; a healthy teammate automatically takes over when one faints.
- Breeding selects two parents and a species from the 151-Pokémon catalog; fusion consumes two creatures, adds generation-based stats, and can be repeated.
- Rival is Nia Vale; the story includes stealing her bike.
- Use Generation I type assignments and interactions; player gear bonuses are attack, defense, and max HP.
- Existing bike theft event says Kanto travel becomes free, but travel must be character-driven rather than destination-button travel.

## Work State
### Completed
- Implemented game shell, campaign progression, battles, recruitment, upgrades, slots and prizes, daycare, fighting club, breeding, repeatable fusion, organization controls, and save migration (`leagueVersion:2`).
- Added 151-species catalog, eight Gym stages, three Victory Road stages, six-creature Elite Four parties and champion party.
- Added badge names (Boulder, Cascade, Thunder, Rainbow, Soul, Marsh, Volcano, Earth); Gym victories explicitly announce earning the badge and badge progress lists earned badge names.
- Expanded `MOVE_ITEMS` in `game.js` to derive from all 50 Generation I TMs and five HMs, including move names, types, source power, approximate eligibility, and HM travel metadata.
- Added gear catalog and `EMPTY_EQUIPMENT` structure; gear behavior and UI are not yet wired.

### Active
- Replace the destination board (`[data-travel]`) and static `drawMap()` with character-driven movement and keyboard/gamepad controls.
- Implement TM/HM inventory, eligibility checks, learning, save persistence, travel actions, and battle moves; HMs must be reusable and usable for travel without badge gates, while TMs are single-use and reobtainable.
- Connect locations, buildings, and caves to world interactions; enforce bike restrictions and faster travel.
- Finish functioning town services, gear shopping, inventory/equipment UI, and combat bonuses.
- Update validation for movement-based travel; run `/tmp/opencode/validate-game.mjs`, test gameplay and save migration, and inspect/update `screenshots/neon-syndicate.jpg` at viewport width ≤1280px.

### Blocked
- (none)

## Next Move
1. Wire `MACHINE_CATALOG`, `HM_CATALOG`, and `MOVE_ITEMS` to shops or item discovery, Pokémon learning, persistent saves, travel actions, and battle moves.
2. Implement continuous character movement and connect buildings, caves, town services, and bike behavior.
3. Finish gear/inventory/equipment and combat bonuses.
4. Update and run validation, test save migration, and inspect/update the screenshot.

## Relevant Files
- `game.js`: Game logic, Gym badges, map/travel, move-machine catalog, town panels, saves, and combat.
- `index.html`: Game shell and interactive UI roots.
- `style.css`: Layout and responsive styling.
- `/tmp/opencode/validate-game.mjs`: Playwright validation script.
- `screenshots/neon-syndicate.jpg`: Existing screenshot to inspect/update.

## Important Context
- Repository changes are uncommitted; tracked game files are untracked (`game.js`, `index.html`, `style.css`, plus supporting files).
- `MACHINE_CATALOG` contains TM01–TM50; `HM_CATALOG` contains HM01–HM05. Learning, inventory, battle, and travel behavior remain unimplemented.
- `renderField()` still renders a destination board with `[data-travel]` buttons; its handler directly changes `state.location`.
- `drawMap()` draws a static canvas; `drawBase()` draws a character sprite but does not enable traversal.
- `INITIAL` includes `insideBuilding`, `bikeMode`, `world:{x:360,y:285}`, and `potions:0`; these are not yet wired into behavior or save migration.

## Findings

- **Move-machine and gear data exists, but the features are not implemented.** In [`game.js`](/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/game.js#L82), lines 82–119 define TM/HM catalogs, move items, and empty equipment data. The inspection found no logic or interface for acquiring machines, teaching moves, or equipping gear.
- **Some related state is already present.** [`game.js`](/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/game.js#L127) lines 127–132 include `bikeMode`, `world`, and equipment in the initial/persisted state, but no corresponding bike or world behavior was found.
- **The scene renders a player, but does not implement movement.** [`game.js`](/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/game.js#L151) lines 151–180 render the base scene and player sprite; controls advertise WASD/arrows and E, while the drawing code reads `walkX`/`walkY`. No handler updates those movement coordinates.
- **Field travel is destination selection, not map movement.** [`game.js`](/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/game.js#L181) lines 181–187 draw a decorative field map that is not shown in the field view. The field view instead uses destination buttons at lines 220–231 to update `state.location` and rerender.
- **Existing bike and Safari actions are limited.** [`game.js`](/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/game.js#L205) lines 205–218 include bike-theft and Safari actions. Bike theft changes a flag and travel label, rather than enabling movement or changing travel mechanics.
- **Keyboard handling has no directional movement.** [`game.js`](/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/game.js#L307) line 307 handles view shortcuts, Escape, and E interactions.
- **The app shell has no dedicated machines or gear interface.** [`index.html`](/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/index.html#L17) lines 17–38 provide navigation, the view root, toast, and modal roots.
- **No focused styling for those interfaces was found.** [`style.css`](/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/style.css#L3) lines 3–6 style destination buttons and the field map; line 8 styles the unrelated Game Corner slot machine.

## Suggested implementation order

1. **Implement field movement first:** connect directional input to player coordinates, add movement bounds/collision as needed, and render the player’s updated position.
2. **Make travel and bike behavior coherent:** decide whether destinations remain a board or become reachable locations, then connect `bikeMode` to actual movement/travel behavior.
3. **Implement machine acquisition and teaching:** use the existing TM/HM catalog and move-item data, with checks for eligibility and available moves.
4. **Add gear management:** expose the existing equipment state through a dedicated interface and make equipped items affect gameplay.
5. **Add focused styling and tests** for the new interactions and persistence.
</subagent>

## Objective
- Complete the pixel RPG’s gameplay systems and make the player name and both rival names editable.

## Requirements
- Keep the game self-contained with localStorage saves using `neon-syndicate-save`.
- Support the campaign, battles, breeding/fusion, equipment, movement-based travel, functioning town services, and usable TMs/HMs.
- Gym victories award named badges; require eight badges and three Victory Road stages before the Elite Four.
- Make the player and both rival names editable.

## Decisions
- Use Generation I Pokémon and type interactions.
- TMs are single-use and reobtainable; HMs are reusable and retain travel abilities without badge gates.
- Existing rival storyline uses Nia Vale; bike theft remains part of the story.

## Work State
### Completed
- Core game shell and campaign systems, 151-species catalog, Gym/Victory Road/Elite Four progression, named badges, TM/HM catalogs, and gear data are present.
- Added `leagueRivalName: 'Nia Vale'` and `crewRivalName: 'Rook Mercer'` defaults to `INITIAL`.
- Updated League rival dialogue, Victory Road story text, Champion display, League summary, and League page description to use `state.leagueRivalName`.
- Updated bike-theft notification text to use the configured League rival name.

### Active
- Add editable controls for player, League rival, and crew rival names; persist names, reject blank values, and use the crew rival name in game content.
- Replace remaining hard-coded League rival references, including the Cerulean bike notice.
- Implement character-driven movement/travel, TM/HM acquisition and use, gear/equipment effects, and functioning town services.
- Update validation, test saves/migration, and inspect/update `screenshots/neon-syndicate.jpg`.

### Blocked
- (none)

## Next Move
1. Add rival-name editing UI and wire it to persisted state; verify player rename behavior and validate nonblank input.
2. Replace remaining hard-coded rival references, then continue movement, TM/HM, equipment, and town-service work.
3. Update and run `/tmp/opencode/validate-game.mjs`; test save migration and inspect the screenshot.

## Relevant Files
- `game.js`: Game state, name editing and references, campaign, movement, machines, gear, and save logic.
- `index.html`: Game shell and existing player rename button.
- `style.css`: Game layout and interaction styling.
- `/tmp/opencode/validate-game.mjs`: Playwright validation.
- `screenshots/neon-syndicate.jpg`: Existing screenshot to inspect or refresh.

## Important Context
- Changes are uncommitted; tracked game files are untracked (`game.js`, `index.html`, `style.css`, plus supporting files).
- Player renaming uses `setName()` and `#rename-btn`; no rival renaming UI exists yet.
- `leagueRivalName` and `crewRivalName` defaults are present, but save loading has not been specifically updated or tested for name migration.
- A targeted edit for the Cerulean bike notice failed because its exact source text did not match; the hard-coded notice remains.
- Movement is not implemented; field travel still uses destination buttons and `drawMap()` is static.
- `MACHINE_CATALOG`, `HM_CATALOG`, and `MOVE_ITEMS` exist, but acquisition, learning, inventory, battle use, and travel actions are unimplemented.

## Objective
- Complete the pixel RPG’s gameplay systems and make the player name and both rival names editable.

## Requirements
- Keep the game self-contained with localStorage saves using `neon-syndicate-save`.
- Support the campaign, battles, breeding/fusion, equipment, movement-based travel, functioning town services, and usable TMs/HMs.
- Gym victories award named badges; require eight badges and three Victory Road stages before the Elite Four.
- Make the player and both rival names editable.

## Decisions
- Use Generation I Pokémon and type interactions.
- TMs are single-use and reobtainable; HMs are reusable and retain travel abilities without badge gates.
- Existing rival storyline uses Nia Vale; bike theft remains part of the story.

## Work State
### Completed
- Core game shell and campaign systems, 151-species catalog, Gym/Victory Road/Elite Four progression, named badges, TM/HM catalogs, and gear data are present.
- Added `leagueRivalName: 'Nia Vale'` and `crewRivalName: 'Rook Mercer'` defaults to `INITIAL`.
- Updated some League dialogue, Victory Road text, Champion display, League summary/page description, and bike-theft notification to use `state.leagueRivalName`.

### Active
- Add editable controls for player, League rival, and crew rival names; persist names, reject blank values, and use the crew rival name in game content.
- Replace remaining hard-coded rival references, including the Cerulean bike notice and Champion/Victory Road names.
- Implement character-driven movement/travel, TM/HM acquisition and use, gear/equipment effects, and functioning town services.
- Update validation, test save migration, and inspect/update `screenshots/neon-syndicate.jpg`.

### Blocked
- (none)

## Next Move
1. Add rival-name editing UI and wire it to persisted state; verify player rename behavior and validate nonblank input.

<subagent sessionID="ses_e46ad6f58ffeiLL4Qv6oaiB75u" state="completed">
## Findings

- **Application wiring:** [index.html](/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/index.html#L34) provides the view, modal, and toast roots, then loads `game.js` at line 40.

- **Travel and movement:** [game.js](/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/game.js#L230) renders a destination board for all ten Kanto locations. Its `[data-travel]` handler directly sets `state.location`, saves, and renders again (line 231), with no HM ownership, eligibility, or destination checks. Although the initial state includes world coordinates and bike-related fields (line 127), the searched code contains no movement controls or world-coordinate travel flow. The bike is a field event; it does not gate the destination board.

- **TM/HM catalog and learning:** `MACHINE_CATALOG`, `HM_CATALOG`, and `MOVE_ITEMS` define TM/HM items, including move data, prices, eligible types, and HM travel descriptions/destinations ([game.js](/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/game.js#L82), lines 94–103). The search found no consumers beyond constructing `MOVE_ITEMS`: there is no acquisition, purchase, or move-learning handler. Thus, the catalog’s HM travel properties are not connected to travel.

- **Equipment:** `PLAYER_SLOTS`, `GEAR`, and `EMPTY_EQUIPMENT` define equipment slots, item stats, and inventory structure ([game.js](/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/game.js#L105)). `load()` validates and restores saved equipment (line 132), but the searched code contains no equipment purchase/equip flow or application of gear stats. The listed gear effects therefore appear to be descriptive data, not active stat modifiers. This is separate from working prize-counter upgrades, which modify creature stats in `buyPrize()` (lines 245–249).

- **Town and related services:** Field wiring supports town-specific gym and League challenges, Safari exploration and business control, roaming trainer challenges and pickpocketing, missions, and the bike event ([game.js](/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/game.js#L231-L239)). Daycare services include paid healing, breeding, and a fighting club; fusion becomes available at higher rank (lines 250–252). These are independent of HM-based travel.

**Main integration risks:** travel is unrestricted direct selection rather than movement- or HM-based; the TM/HM catalog has no learning/acquisition path; and gear is saved but not visibly applied.
</subagent>

## Objective
- Complete the pixel RPG’s gameplay systems and make the player name and both rival names editable.

## Requirements
- Keep the game self-contained with localStorage saves using `neon-syndicate-save`.
- Support the campaign, battles, breeding/fusion, equipment, movement-based travel, functioning town services, and usable TMs/HMs.
- Gym victories award named badges; require eight badges and three Victory Road stages before the Elite Four.
- Make the player and both rival names editable.

## Decisions
- Use Generation I Pokémon and type interactions.
- TMs are single-use and reobtainable; HMs are reusable and retain travel abilities without badge gates.
- Existing rival storyline uses Nia Vale; bike theft remains part of the story.

## Work State
### Completed
- Core game shell and campaign systems, 151-species catalog, Gym/Victory Road/Elite Four progression, named badges, TM/HM catalogs, and gear data are present.
- Added `leagueRivalName: 'Nia Vale'` and `crewRivalName: 'Rook Mercer'` defaults to `INITIAL`.
- Some League dialogue, Victory Road text, Champion display, League summary/page description, and bike-theft notification use `state.leagueRivalName`.

### Active
- Add editable controls for player, League rival, and crew rival names; persist names, reject blank values, and use the crew rival name in game content.
- Replace remaining hard-coded rival references, including the Cerulean bike notice and Champion/Victory Road names.
- Implement character-driven movement/travel, TM/HM acquisition and use, gear/equipment effects, and functioning town services.
- Update validation, test save migration, and inspect/update `screenshots/neon-syndicate.jpg`.

### Blocked
- (none)

## Next Move
1. Add rival-name editing UI and wire it to persisted state; verify player rename behavior and validate nonblank input.
2. Replace remaining hard-coded rival references, then continue movement, TM/HM, equipment, and town-service work.
3. Update and run `/tmp/opencode/validate-game.mjs`; test save migration and inspect the screenshot.

## Relevant Files
- `game.js`: State, save loading, names, campaign, movement, machines, gear, and town services.
- `index.html`: Game shell and existing player rename button.
- `style.css`: Game layout and interaction styling.
- `/tmp/opencode/validate-game.mjs`: Playwright validation.
- `screenshots/neon-syndicate.jpg`: Existing screenshot to inspect or refresh.

## Important Context
- Changes are uncommitted; tracked game files are untracked (`game.js`, `index.html`, `style.css`, plus supporting files).
- Player renaming uses `setName()` and `#rename-btn`; no rival renaming UI exists yet.
- `leagueRivalName` and `crewRivalName` defaults exist, but save loading has not been specifically updated or tested for name migration.
- A targeted edit for the Cerulean bike notice failed because its exact source text did not match; the hard-coded notice remains.
- Movement is not implemented; field travel still uses destination buttons and `drawMap()` is static.
- `MACHINE_CATALOG`, `HM_CATALOG`, and `MOVE_ITEMS` exist, but acquisition, learning, inventory, battle use, and travel actions are unimplemented.
- `VICTORY_ROAD` entries and `CHAMPION` still contain hard-coded Nia names; `leagueStage()` dynamically substitutes the League rival name in some story text.

messages.summary:
## Objective
- Complete the pixel RPG’s gameplay systems and make the player name and both rival names editable.

## Requirements
- Keep the game self-contained with localStorage saves using `neon-syndicate-save`.
- Support the campaign, battles, breeding/fusion, equipment, movement-based travel, functioning town services, and usable TMs/HMs.
- Gym victories award named badges; require eight badges and three Victory Road stages before the Elite Four.
- Make the player and both rival names editable.

## Decisions
- Use Generation I Pokémon and type interactions.
- TMs are single-use and reobtainable; HMs are reusable and retain travel abilities without badge gates.
- Existing rival storyline uses Nia Vale; bike theft remains part of the story.

## Work State
### Completed
- Core game shell and campaign systems, 151-species catalog, Gym/Victory Road/Elite Four progression, named badges, TM/HM catalogs, and gear data are present.
- `INITIAL` includes `leagueRivalName: 'Nia Vale'` and `crewRivalName: 'Rook Mercer'`.
- Some League dialogue, Victory Road text, Champion display, League summary/page description, and bike-theft notification use `state.leagueRivalName`.

### Active
- Add editable controls for player, League rival, and crew rival names; persist names, reject blank values, and use the crew rival name in game content.
- Replace remaining hard-coded rival references, including the Cerulean bike notice and Victory Road/Champion names.
- Implement character-driven movement/travel, TM/HM acquisition and use, gear/equipment effects, and functioning town services.
- Update validation, test save migration, and inspect/update `screenshots/neon-syndicate.jpg`.

### Blocked
- (none)

## Next Move
1. Add rival-name editing UI and wire it to persisted state; verify player rename behavior and validate nonblank input.
2. Replace remaining hard-coded rival references, then continue movement, TM/HM, equipment, and town-service work.
3. Update and run `/tmp/opencode/validate-game.mjs`; test save migration and inspect the screenshot.

## Relevant Files
- `game.js`: State, save loading, names, campaign, movement, machines, gear, and town services.
- `index.html`: Game shell and existing player rename button.
- `style.css`: Game layout and interaction styling.
- `/tmp/opencode/validate-game.mjs`: Playwright validation.
- `screenshots/neon-syndicate.jpg`: Existing screenshot to inspect or refresh.

## Important Context
- Changes are uncommitted; tracked game files are untracked (`game.js`, `index.html`, `style.css`, plus supporting files).
- Player renaming uses `setName()` and `#rename-btn`; no rival renaming UI exists yet.
- `leagueRivalName` and `crewRivalName` defaults exist, but save loading has not been specifically updated or tested for name migration.
- A targeted edit for the Cerulean bike notice failed because its exact source text did not match; the hard-coded notice remains.
- Movement is not implemented; field travel still uses destination buttons and `drawMap()` is static.
- `MACHINE_CATALOG`, `HM_CATALOG`, and `MOVE_ITEMS` exist, but acquisition, learning, inventory, battle use, and travel actions are unimplemented.
- `VICTORY_ROAD` entries and `CHAMPION` still contain hard-coded Nia names; `leagueStage()` dynamically substitutes the League rival name in some story text.
- Code inspection identified `game.js` lines 230–231 as direct destination travel wiring; no movement controls or world-coordinate travel flow were found.

## Objective
- Complete the pixel RPG’s gameplay systems and make the player name and both rival names editable.

## Requirements
- Keep the game self-contained with localStorage saves using `neon-syndicate-save`.
- Support the campaign, battles, breeding/fusion, equipment, movement-based travel, functioning town services, and usable TMs/HMs.
- Gym victories award named badges; require eight badges and three Victory Road stages before the Elite Four.
- Make the player and both rival names editable.

## Decisions
- Use Generation I Pokémon and type interactions.
- TMs are single-use and reobtainable; HMs are reusable and retain travel abilities without badge gates.
- Existing rival storyline uses Nia Vale; bike theft remains part of the story.

## Work State
### Completed
- Core game shell and campaign systems, 151-species catalog, Gym/Victory Road/Elite Four progression, named badges, TM/HM catalogs, and gear data are present.
- `INITIAL` includes `leagueRivalName: 'Nia Vale'` and `crewRivalName: 'Rook Mercer'`.
- Some League dialogue, Victory Road text, Champion display, League summary/page description, and bike-theft notification use `state.leagueRivalName`.

### Active
- Add editable controls for player, League rival, and crew rival names; persist names, reject blank values, and use the crew rival name in game content.
- Replace remaining hard-coded rival references, including the Cerulean bike notice and Victory Road/Champion names.
- Implement character-driven movement/travel, TM/HM acquisition and use, gear/equipment effects, and functioning town services.
- Update validation, test save migration, and inspect/update `screenshots/neon-syndicate.jpg`.

### Blocked
- (none)

## Next Move
1. Add rival-name editing UI and wire it to persisted state; verify player rename behavior and validate nonblank input.
2. Replace remaining hard-coded rival references, then continue movement, TM/HM, equipment, and town-service work.
3. Update and run `/tmp/opencode/validate-game.mjs`; test save migration and inspect the screenshot.

## Relevant Files
- `game.js`: State, save loading, names, campaign, movement, machines, gear, and town services.
- `index.html`: Game shell and existing player rename button.
- `style.css`: Game layout and interaction styling.
- `/tmp/opencode/validate-game.mjs`: Playwright validation.
- `screenshots/neon-syndicate.jpg`: Existing screenshot to inspect or refresh.

## Important Context
- Changes are uncommitted; tracked game files are untracked (`game.js`, `index.html`, `style.css`, plus supporting files).
- Player renaming uses `setName()` and `#rename-btn`; no rival renaming UI exists yet.
- `leagueRivalName` and `crewRivalName` defaults exist, but save loading has not been specifically updated or tested for name migration.
- A targeted edit for the Cerulean bike notice failed because its exact source text did not match; the hard-coded notice remains.
- Movement is not implemented; field travel still uses destination buttons and `drawMap()` is static.
- `MACHINE_CATALOG`, `HM_CATALOG`, and `MOVE_ITEMS` exist, but acquisition, learning, inventory, battle use, and travel actions are unimplemented.
- `VICTORY_ROAD` entries and `CHAMPION` still contain hard-coded Nia names; `leagueStage()` dynamically substitutes the League rival name in some story text.

messages.summary:
## Objective
- Complete the pixel RPG’s gameplay systems and make the player name and both rival names editable.

## Requirements
- Keep the game self-contained with localStorage saves using `neon-syndicate-save`.
- Support the campaign, battles, breeding/fusion, equipment, movement-based travel, functioning town services, and usable TMs/HMs.
- Gym victories award named badges; require eight badges and three Victory Road stages before the Elite Four.
- Make the player and both rival names editable.

## Decisions
- Use Generation I Pokémon and type interactions.
- TMs are single-use and reobtainable; HMs are reusable and retain travel abilities without badge gates.
- Existing rival storyline uses Nia Vale; bike theft remains part of the story.

## Work State
### Completed
- Core game shell and campaign systems, 151-species catalog, Gym/Victory Road/Elite Four progression, named badges, TM/HM catalogs, and gear data are present.
- `INITIAL` defines `leagueRivalName: 'Nia Vale'` and `crewRivalName: 'Rook Mercer'`.
- Some League dialogue, Victory Road text, Champion display, League summary/page description, and bike-theft notification use `state.leagueRivalName`.

### Active
- Add editable controls for player, League rival, and crew rival names; persist names, reject blank values, and verify player rename behavior.
- Replace remaining hard-coded rival references, including the Cerulean bike notice and Victory Road/Champion names; use the crew rival name in game content.
- Implement character-driven movement/travel, TM/HM acquisition and use, gear/equipment effects, and functioning town services.
- Update validation, test save migration, and inspect/update `screenshots/neon-syndicate.jpg`.

### Blocked
- (none)

## Next Move
1. Add rival-name editing UI and wire it to persisted state; validate nonblank input and save migration.
2. Replace remaining hard-coded rival references, then continue movement, TM/HM, equipment, and town-service work.
3. Update and run `/tmp/opencode/validate-game.mjs`; inspect and refresh the screenshot if needed.

## Relevant Files
- `game.js`: State, save loading, names, campaign, movement, machines, gear, and town services.
- `index.html`: Game shell and existing player rename button.
- `style.css`: Game layout and interaction styling.
- `/tmp/opencode/validate-game.mjs`: Playwright validation.
- `screenshots/neon-syndicate.jpg`: Existing screenshot to inspect or refresh.

## Important Context
- Changes are uncommitted; tracked game files are untracked (`game.js`, `index.html`, `style.css`, plus supporting files).
- Player renaming uses `setName()` and `#rename-btn`; no rival renaming UI exists yet.
- Rival name defaults exist, but save loading has not been specifically updated or tested for name migration.
- A targeted edit for the Cerulean bike notice failed because its exact source text did not match; the hard-coded notice remains.
- Movement is not implemented; field travel still uses destination buttons and `drawMap()` is static.
- `MACHINE_CATALOG`, `HM_CATALOG`, and `MOVE_ITEMS` exist, but acquisition, learning, inventory, battle use, and travel actions are unimplemented.
- `VICTORY_ROAD` entries and `CHAMPION` still contain hard-coded Nia names; `leagueStage()` dynamically substitutes the League rival name in some story text.

messages.summary:
## Objective
- Complete the pixel RPG’s gameplay systems and make the player name and both rival names editable.

## Requirements
- Keep the game self-contained with localStorage saves using `neon-syndicate-save`.
- Support the campaign, battles, breeding/fusion, equipment, movement-based travel, functioning town services, and usable TMs/HMs.
- Gym victories award named badges; require eight badges and three Victory Road stages before the Elite Four.
- Make the player and both rival names editable.

## Decisions
- Use Generation I Pokémon and type interactions.
- TMs are single-use and reobtainable; HMs are reusable and retain travel abilities without badge gates.
- Existing rival storyline uses Nia Vale; bike theft remains part of the story.

## Work State
### Completed
- Core game shell and campaign systems, 151-species catalog, Gym/Victory Road/Elite Four progression, named badges, TM/HM catalogs, and gear data are present.
- `INITIAL` defines `leagueRivalName: 'Nia Vale'` and `crewRivalName: 'Rook Mercer'`.
- Some League dialogue, Victory Road text, Champion display, League summary/page description, and bike-theft notification use `state.leagueRivalName`.

### Active
- Add editable controls for player, League rival, and crew rival names; persist names, reject blank values, and verify player rename behavior.
- Replace remaining hard-coded rival references, including the Cerulean bike notice, Victory Road/Champion names; use the crew rival name in game content.
- Implement character-driven movement/travel, TM/HM acquisition and use, gear/equipment effects, and functioning town services.
- Update validation, test save migration, and inspect/update `screenshots/neon-syndicate.jpg`.

### Blocked
- (none)

## Next Move
1. Add rival-name editing UI and wire it to persisted state; validate nonblank input and save migration.
2. Replace remaining hard-coded rival references, then continue movement, TM/HM, equipment, and town-service work.
3. Update and run `/tmp/opencode/validate-game.mjs`; inspect and refresh the screenshot if needed.

## Relevant Files
- `game.js`: State, save loading, names, campaign, movement, machines, gear, and town services.
- `index.html`: Game shell and existing player rename button.
- `style.css`: Game layout and interaction styling.
- `/tmp/opencode/validate-game.mjs`: Playwright validation.
- `screenshots/neon-syndicate.jpg`: Existing screenshot to inspect or refresh.

## Important Context
- Changes are uncommitted; tracked game files are untracked (`game.js`, `index.html`, `style.css`, plus supporting files).
- Player renaming uses `setName()` and `#rename-btn`; no rival renaming UI exists yet.
- Rival name defaults exist, but save loading has not been specifically updated or tested for name migration.
- A targeted edit for the Cerulean bike notice failed because its exact source text did not match; the hard-coded notice remains.
- Movement is not implemented; field travel still uses destination buttons and `drawMap()` is static.
- `MACHINE_CATALOG`, `HM_CATALOG`, and `MOVE_ITEMS` exist, but acquisition, learning, inventory, battle use, and travel actions are unimplemented.
- `VICTORY_ROAD` entries and `CHAMPION` still contain hard-coded Nia names; `leagueStage()` dynamically substitutes the League rival name in some story text.

## Objective
- Complete the pixel RPG’s gameplay systems and make the player name and both rival names editable.
- Make map trainer battles repeatable after a cooldown measured in steps walked.

## Requirements
- Keep the game self-contained with localStorage saves using `neon-syndicate-save`.
- Support the campaign, battles, breeding/fusion, equipment, movement-based travel, functioning town services, and usable TMs/HMs.
- Gym victories award named badges; require eight badges and three Victory Road stages before the Elite Four.
- Make the player and both rival names editable.
- Allow map trainer battles to become available again after the player walks a cooldown number of steps.

## Decisions
- Use Generation I Pokémon and type interactions.
- TMs are single-use and reobtainable; HMs are reusable and retain travel abilities without badge gates.
- Existing rival storyline uses Nia Vale; bike theft remains part of the story.

- Core game shell and campaign systems, 151-species catalog, Gym/Victory Road/Elite Four progression, named badges, TM/HM catalogs, and gear data are present.

- Replace remaining hard-coded rival references and use the crew rival name in game content.
- Implement walking-based trainer cooldowns and repeatable map battles.
- Implement character-driven movement/travel, TM/HM acquisition and use, equipment effects, and functioning town services.
- Update validation, test save migration and rename behavior, and inspect/update `screenshots/neon-syndicate.jpg`.

- Existing validation fails at `/tmp/opencode/validate-game.mjs:22`: `locator.click: Timeout 30000ms exceeded`, waiting for `#steal-bike` after traveling to Cerulean City.

1: ## Process lifecycle
2: 
3: - Run long-lived servers and watchers in a persistent session such as tmux.
4: - Do not background them in bounded commands without explicit detachment and cleanup.
5: - After a timeout, inspect the process and endpoint before retrying or claiming failure.
6: 
7: ## Linux browser and WebGPU capture
8: 
9: - Use the preinstalled `playwright-cli` executable from Actions or SSH.
10: - Use its headed Chromium, persistent Xvfb display, and SwiftShader configuration.
11: - Run `playwright-cli open http://localhost:3002` for the Pascal development server.
12: - Load a saved scene. Wait for actual geometry and the active WebGPU renderer.
13: - Run `playwright-cli screenshot --filename=screenshots/linux.png` after creating the output directory.
14: - Inspect the image. Reject loading screens, empty grids, and blank canvases.
15: - Report SwiftShader as CPU software rendering. Do not claim GPU hardware acceleration.
16: - Inspect `$HOME/.local/share/omgithub-playwright/linux.json` for launch settings.
17: - Use `playwright-cli --help` for commands and named sessions. Pass configuration only to `open`.
18: 
19: ## Mobile browser games
20: 
21: - Support Android and iOS phones and tablets with responsive layouts and usable touch controls.
22: - Keep gameplay and controls visible within safe areas and avoid browser gesture conflicts.
23: - Add tilt controls only when appropriate; offer touch alternatives and request iOS motion permission from a user gesture when needed.
24: - Follow explicit device and control requirements in the user request.

3: - Run long-lived servers and watchers in a persistent session such as tmux.
4: - Do not background them in bounded commands without explicit detachment and cleanup.
5: - After a timeout, inspect the process and endpoint before retrying or claiming failure.
6: 
7: ## Linux browser and WebGPU capture
8: 
9: - Use the preinstalled `playwright-cli` executable from Actions or SSH.
10: - Use its headed Chromium, persistent Xvfb display, and SwiftShader configuration.

## Objective
- Complete the pixel RPG’s gameplay systems and add editable player and rival names.
- Render a traversable field map with varied, area-appropriate trainers whose battles become available again after walking-based cooldowns.

## Requirements
- Keep the game self-contained with localStorage saves using `neon-syndicate-save`.
- Support campaign, battles, breeding/fusion, equipment, movement-based travel, town services, and usable TMs/HMs.
- Gym victories award named badges; require eight badges and three Victory Road stages before the Elite Four.
- Allow editing the player name and both rival names.
- Match locations to source material, make all routes traversable, and provide varied numbers of trainers per location; trainers may be randomized, but Pokémon levels must suit each area.

## Decisions
- Use Generation I Pokémon and type interactions.
- TMs are single-use and reobtainable; HMs are reusable and retain travel abilities without badge gates.
- Existing rival storyline uses Nia Vale; bike theft remains part of the story.
- The second rival’s default name is Rook Mercer.

## Work State
### Completed
- Core game shell and campaign systems, 151-species catalog, League progression, named badges, TM/HM catalogs, and gear data are present.
- Player rename uses `setName()` and `#rename-btn`; blank names are rejected and values are saved.

### Active
- Wire `drawMap()` into a rendered field map; implement keyboard movement and persisted step tracking.
- Add source-aligned, fully traversable routes and locations with varied randomized trainer counts and area-scaled Pokémon levels.
- Re-enable defeated map trainers after a walking cooldown.
- Add rival-name editing and replace remaining hard-coded rival references, including Victory Road entries and Champion name.
- Implement TM/HM acquisition and use, equipment effects, and functioning town services.
- Update validation, test save migration and rename behavior, and inspect/update `screenshots/neon-syndicate.jpg`.

### Blocked
- `/tmp/opencode/validate-game.mjs` times out waiting for `#steal-bike` after traveling to Cerulean City.

## Next Move
1. Add the field map UI, keyboard movement, persisted step tracking, and walking-based trainer cooldowns.
2. Expand map routes to match source material, ensure every route is traversable, and distribute varied area-level trainers.
3. Add rival-name editing and replace hard-coded rival references.
4. Continue TM/HM, equipment, and town-service implementation.
5. Fix and run `/tmp/opencode/validate-game.mjs`; inspect and refresh the screenshot if needed.

## Relevant Files
- `game.js`: Save migration, field travel, trainer battles, campaign, map drawing, and event handlers.
- `index.html`: Game shell and player rename control.
- `style.css`: Game layout and interaction styling.
- `/tmp/opencode/validate-game.mjs`: Playwright validation script.
- `screenshots/neon-syndicate.jpg`: Existing screenshot to inspect or refresh.

## Important Context
- Changes are uncommitted; tracked game files are untracked (`game.js`, `index.html`, `style.css`, plus supporting files).
- `drawMap()` exists but `renderField()` does not render a map canvas or call it.
- A document `keydown` handler exists for navigation and interactions, but field walking is not implemented.
- Map travel currently changes `state.location` immediately from `[data-travel]` buttons; `INITIAL` has `world:{x:360,y:285}` but no step counter.

- `load()` defaults `leagueRivalName` and `crewRivalName` via `INITIAL`, but rival renaming is not implemented.

## Objective
- Complete the pixel RPG’s gameplay systems and add editable player and rival names.
- Render a traversable field map with varied, area-appropriate trainers whose battles become available again after walking-based cooldowns.

## Requirements
- Keep the game self-contained with localStorage saves using `neon-syndicate-save`.
- Support campaign, battles, breeding/fusion, equipment, movement-based travel, town services, and usable TMs/HMs.
- Gym victories award named badges; require eight badges and three Victory Road stages before the Elite Four.
- Allow editing the player name and both rival names.
- Match locations to source material, make all routes traversable, and provide varied numbers of trainers per location with area-appropriate levels.

## Decisions
- Use Generation I Pokémon and type interactions.
- TMs are single-use and reobtainable; HMs are reusable and retain travel abilities without badge gates.
- Existing rival storyline uses Nia Vale; bike theft remains part of the story.
- The second rival’s default name is Rook Mercer.

## Work State
### Completed
- Core game shell and campaign systems, 151-species catalog, League progression, named badges, TM/HM catalogs, and gear data are present.
- Player rename uses `setName()` and `#rename-btn`; blank names are rejected and values are saved.

### Active
- Wire `drawMap()` into a rendered field map; implement keyboard movement and persisted step tracking.
- Add source-aligned, fully traversable routes and locations with varied randomized trainer counts and area-scaled Pokémon levels.
- Re-enable defeated map trainers after a walking cooldown.
- Add rival-name editing and replace remaining hard-coded rival references, including Victory Road entries and Champion name.
- Implement TM/HM acquisition and use, equipment effects, and functioning town services.
- Update validation, test save migration and rename behavior, and inspect/update `screenshots/neon-syndicate.jpg`.

### Blocked
- `/tmp/opencode/validate-game.mjs` times out waiting for `#steal-bike` after traveling to Cerulean City.

## Next Move
1. Add the field map UI, keyboard movement, persisted step tracking, and walking-based trainer cooldowns.
2. Expand map routes to match source material, ensure every route is traversable, and distribute varied area-level trainers.
3. Add rival-name editing and replace hard-coded rival references.
4. Continue TM/HM, equipment, and town-service implementation.
5. Fix and run `/tmp/opencode/validate-game.mjs`; inspect and refresh the screenshot if needed.

## Relevant Files
- `game.js`: Save migration, field travel, trainer battles, campaign, map drawing, and event handlers.
- `index.html`: Game shell and player rename control.
- `style.css`: Game layout and interaction styling.
- `/tmp/opencode/validate-game.mjs`: Playwright validation script.
- `screenshots/neon-syndicate.jpg`: Existing screenshot to inspect or refresh.

## Important Context
- Changes are uncommitted; tracked game files are untracked (`game.js`, `index.html`, `style.css`, plus supporting files).
- `drawMap()` exists but `renderField()` does not render a map canvas or call it.
- A document `keydown` handler exists for navigation and interactions, but field walking is not implemented.
- Map travel currently changes `state.location` immediately from `[data-travel]` buttons; `INITIAL` has `world:{x:360,y:285}` but no step counter.
- `fieldTrainer()` creates one trainer per location with `defeated:false`; `startMapTrainer()` rejects defeated trainers, and `finishBattle()` permanently sets `state.trainers[b.id].defeated=true`.
- `load()` defaults `leagueRivalName` and `crewRivalName` via `INITIAL`, but rival renaming is not implemented.
- Validation navigates to `http://localhost:3000/`, starts the game and starter selection, then times out waiting for `#steal-bike` after selecting Cerulean City.

## Objective
- Complete the pixel RPG’s gameplay systems and add editable player and rival names.
- Render a traversable Kanto field map with varied, area-appropriate trainers that return after walking-based cooldowns.

## Requirements
- Keep the game self-contained with localStorage saves using `neon-syndicate-save`.
- Support campaign, battles, breeding/fusion, equipment, movement-based travel, town services, and usable TMs/HMs.
- Gym victories award named badges; require eight badges and three Victory Road stages before the Elite Four.
- Allow editing the player name and both rival names.
- Match locations to source material, make routes traversable, and distribute varied trainers with area-appropriate levels.

## Decisions
- Use Generation I Pokémon and type interactions.
- TMs are single-use and reobtainable; HMs are reusable and retain travel abilities without badge gates.
- Existing rival storyline uses Nia Vale; bike theft remains part of the story.
- The second rival’s default name is Rook Mercer.

## Work State
### Completed
- Core game shell and campaign systems, 151-species catalog, League progression, named badges, TM/HM catalogs, and gear data are present.
- Player rename uses `setName()` and `#rename-btn`; blank names are rejected and values are saved.

### Active
- Wire `drawMap()` into a rendered field map; implement keyboard movement and persisted step tracking.
- Expand routes, ensure traversability, and distribute varied area-level trainers.
- Re-enable defeated map trainers after a walking cooldown.
- Add rival-name editing and replace hard-coded rival references, including Victory Road entries and Champion name.
- Implement TM/HM acquisition and use, equipment effects, and functioning town services.
- Update validation, test save migration and rename behavior, and inspect/update `screenshots/neon-syndicate.jpg`.

### Blocked
- `/tmp/opencode/validate-game.mjs` times out waiting for `#steal-bike` after traveling to Cerulean City.

## Next Move
1. Add the field map UI, keyboard movement, persisted step tracking, and walking-based trainer cooldowns.
2. Expand routes and distribute varied, area-appropriate trainers.
3. Add rival-name editing and replace hard-coded rival references.
4. Continue TM/HM, equipment, and town-service implementation.
5. Fix and run `/tmp/opencode/validate-game.mjs`; inspect and refresh the screenshot if needed.

## Relevant Files
- `game.js`: Save migration, field travel, trainer battles, campaign, map drawing, and event handlers.
- `index.html`: Game shell and player rename control.
- `style.css`: Game layout and interaction styling.
- `/tmp/opencode/validate-game.mjs`: Playwright validation script.
- `screenshots/neon-syndicate.jpg`: Existing screenshot to inspect or refresh.

## Important Context
- Changes are uncommitted; tracked game files are untracked (`game.js`, `index.html`, `style.css`, plus supporting files).
- `drawMap()` exists but `renderField()` does not render a map canvas or call it.
- A document `keydown` handler exists for navigation and interactions, but field walking is not implemented.
- Map travel currently changes `state.location` immediately from `[data-travel]` buttons; `INITIAL` has `world:{x:360,y:285}` but no step counter.
- `fieldTrainer()` creates one trainer per location with `defeated:false`; `startMapTrainer()` rejects defeated trainers, and `finishBattle()` permanently sets `state.trainers[b.id].defeated=true`.
- `load()` defaults `leagueRivalName` and `crewRivalName` via `INITIAL`, but rival renaming is not implemented.
