## Objective
- Complete the pixel RPG’s gameplay systems and add editable player and rival names.
- Render a traversable Kanto map with varied, area-appropriate trainers that return after walking-based cooldowns; ensure TM/HM battle moves match their source materials.

## Requirements
- Keep the game self-contained with localStorage saves using `neon-syndicate-save`.
- Support campaign, battles, breeding/fusion, equipment, movement-based travel, town services, and usable TMs/HMs.
- Gym victories award named badges; require eight badges and three Victory Road stages before the Elite Four.
- Allow editing the player name and both rival names.
- Match locations to source material, make routes traversable, and distribute varied trainers with area-appropriate levels.
- Use source-accurate TM/HM battle move data.

## Decisions
- Use Generation I Pokémon and type interactions.
- TMs are single-use and reobtainable; HMs are reusable and retain travel abilities without badge gates.
- Existing rival storyline uses Nia Vale; bike theft remains part of the story.
- The second rival’s default name is Rook Mercer.

## Work State
### Completed
- Core game shell and campaign systems, 151-species catalog, League progression, named badges, TM/HM catalogs, and gear data are present.
- Player rename uses `setName()` and `#rename-btn`; blank names are rejected and values are saved.
- `drawMap()` exists and paints a basic field scene.

### Active
- Wire `drawMap()` into a rendered field map; implement keyboard movement and persisted step tracking.
- Expand routes, ensure traversability, and distribute varied area-level trainers.
- Re-enable defeated map trainers after a walking cooldown.
- Add rival-name editing and replace hard-coded rival references, including Victory Road entries and Champion name.
- Implement TM/HM acquisition and use with source-accurate battle move data, equipment effects, and functioning town services.
- Update validation, test save migration and rename behavior, and inspect/update `screenshots/neon-syndicate.jpg`.

### Blocked
- `/tmp/opencode/validate-game.mjs` times out waiting for `#steal-bike` after traveling to Cerulean City.

## Next Move
1. Add the field map UI, keyboard movement, persisted step tracking, and walking-based trainer cooldowns.
2. Expand routes and distribute varied, area-appropriate trainers.
3. Add rival-name editing and replace hard-coded rival references.
4. Implement TM/HM acquisition and use; correct battle move data to match source materials; complete equipment and town services.
5. Fix and run `/tmp/opencode/validate-game.mjs`; inspect and refresh the screenshot if needed.

## Relevant Files
- `game.js`: Game state, map drawing, trainers, campaign, TM/HM catalog, battles, and event handlers.
- `index.html`: Game shell and player rename control.
- `style.css`: Game layout and interaction styling.
- `/tmp/opencode/validate-game.mjs`: Playwright validation script.
- `screenshots/neon-syndicate.jpg`: Existing screenshot to inspect or refresh.

## Important Context
- Changes are uncommitted; tracked game files are untracked (`game.js`, `index.html`, `style.css`, plus supporting files).
- `drawMap()` exists, but `renderField()` does not render a map canvas or call it.
- A document `keydown` handler exists for navigation and interactions, but field walking is not implemented.
- Map travel currently changes `state.location` immediately from `[data-travel]` buttons; `INITIAL` has `world:{x:360,y:285}` but no step counter.
- `fieldTrainer()` creates one trainer per location with `defeated:false`; `startMapTrainer()` rejects defeated trainers, and `finishBattle()` permanently sets `state.trainers[b.id].defeated=true`.
- `MOVE_ITEMS` derives battle `power` by scaling `sourcePower` (`Math.round(sourcePower/7)`) and assigns each TM only its listed type as eligibility; source-accurate move behavior/data remains to be implemented.

## Objective
- Complete the pixel RPG’s gameplay systems and add editable player and rival names.
- Render a traversable Kanto map with varied, area-appropriate trainers that return after walking-based cooldowns; ensure TM/HM battle moves match their source materials.

## Requirements
- Keep the game self-contained with localStorage saves using `neon-syndicate-save`.
- Support campaign, battles, breeding/fusion, equipment, movement-based travel, town services, and usable TMs/HMs.
- Gym victories award named badges; require eight badges and three Victory Road stages before the Elite Four.
- Allow editing the player name and both rival names.
- Match locations to source material, make routes traversable, and distribute varied trainers with area-appropriate levels.
- Use Generation I Pokémon and type interactions; make TMs single-use and reobtainable, HMs reusable, and keep HM travel abilities ungated by badges.

## Decisions
- Use Generation I Pokémon and type interactions.
- Existing rival storyline uses Nia Vale; bike theft remains part of the story.
- The second rival’s default name is Rook Mercer.

## Work State
### Completed
- Core game shell and campaign systems, 151-species catalog, League progression, named badges, TM/HM catalogs, and gear data are present.
- Player rename uses `setName()` and `#rename-btn`; blank names are rejected and values are saved.
- `drawMap()` exists and paints a basic field scene.

### Active
- Render `drawMap()` in the field UI; implement keyboard movement and persisted step tracking.
- Expand routes, ensure traversability, and distribute varied area-level trainers.
- Re-enable defeated map trainers after a walking cooldown.
- Add rival-name editing and replace hard-coded rival references, including Victory Road entries and Champion name.
- Implement TM/HM acquisition and use with source-accurate battle move data; complete equipment effects and town services.
- Update validation, test save migration and rename behavior, and inspect/update `screenshots/neon-syndicate.jpg`.

### Blocked
- `/tmp/opencode/validate-game.mjs` times out waiting for `#steal-bike` after traveling to Cerulean City.

## Next Move
1. Add the field map UI, keyboard movement, persisted step tracking, and walking-based trainer cooldowns.
2. Expand routes and distribute varied, area-appropriate trainers.
3. Add rival-name editing and replace hard-coded rival references.
4. Implement TM/HM acquisition and use; correct battle move data to match source materials; complete equipment and town services.
5. Fix and run `/tmp/opencode/validate-game.mjs`; inspect and refresh the screenshot if needed.

## Relevant Files
- `/tmp/opencode/validate-game.mjs`: Playwright validation script.
- `game.js`: Game logic, campaign systems, map drawing, trainers, and TM/HM data.
- `index.html`: Game shell and DOM structure.
- `style.css`: Game styling.

## Important Context
- Changes are uncommitted; tracked game files are untracked (`game.js`, `index.html`, `style.css`, plus supporting files).
- `drawMap()` exists, but `renderField()` does not render a map canvas or call it.
- A document `keydown` handler exists for navigation and interactions, but field walking is not implemented.
- Map travel currently changes `state.location` immediately from `[data-travel]` buttons; `INITIAL` has `world:{x:360,y:285}` but no step counter.
- `fieldTrainer()` creates one trainer per location with `defeated:false`; `startMapTrainer()` rejects defeated trainers, and `finishBattle()` permanently sets `state.trainers[b.id].defeated=true`.
- `MOVE_ITEMS` derives battle `power` by scaling `sourcePower` (`Math.round(sourcePower/7)`) and assigns each TM only its listed type as eligibility; source-accurate move behavior/data remains to be implemented.

messages.summary:
## Objective
- Complete the pixel RPG’s gameplay systems and add editable player and rival names.
- Ensure defeated player Pokémon cause a blackout and return the player to base.

## Requirements
- Keep the game self-contained with localStorage saves using `neon-syndicate-save`.
- Support campaign, battles, breeding/fusion, equipment, movement-based travel, town services, and usable TMs/HMs.
- Gym victories award named badges; require eight badges and three Victory Road stages before the Elite Four.
- Allow editing the player name and both rival names.
- Match locations to source material, make routes traversable, and distribute varied trainers with area-appropriate levels.
- Re-enable defeated map trainers after a walking cooldown.
- Use Generation I Pokémon and type interactions; make TMs single-use and reobtainable, HMs reusable, and keep HM travel abilities ungated by badges.
- Bike theft should occur after beating the protagonist’s rival upon meeting them in Cerulean City.
- If all player Pokémon are defeated, the player blacks out and wakes up at base.

## Decisions
- Use Generation I Pokémon and type interactions.
- Existing rival storyline uses Nia Vale; bike theft remains part of the story, triggered after defeating the protagonist’s rival in Cerulean City.
- The second rival’s default name is Rook Mercer.

## Work State
### Completed
- Core game shell and campaign systems, 151-species catalog, League progression, named badges, TM/HM catalogs, and gear data are present.
- Player rename uses `setName()` and `#rename-btn`; blank names are rejected and values are saved.
- `drawMap()` paints a basic field scene.
- `leagueStage()` uses `state.leagueRivalName` for Victory Road and Champion references.

### Active
- Implement blackout behavior when no player Pokémon remain able to battle, returning the player to base.
- Render `drawMap()` in the field UI; implement keyboard movement and persisted step tracking.
- Expand routes, ensure traversability, and distribute varied area-level trainers.
- Re-enable defeated map trainers after a walking cooldown.
- Add rival-name editing and replace hard-coded rival references; make the Cerulean City rival victory trigger bike theft.
- Implement TM/HM acquisition and use; correct battle move data to match source materials; complete equipment and town services.
- Diagnose the validation timeout, then run `/tmp/opencode/validate-game.mjs` and inspect the screenshot if needed.

### Blocked
- `/tmp/opencode/validate-game.mjs` times out waiting for `#steal-bike` after traveling to Cerulean City; root cause remains undiagnosed.

## Next Move
1. Implement the blackout flow in `battleTurn()` when all team Pokémon have fainted: return to base and handle recovery consistently.
2. Continue field map, movement, trainer cooldown, route, and rival requirements.
3. Diagnose the existing validation timeout and run the validation script.

## Relevant Files
- `game.js`: Game logic, campaign systems, battle resolution, map drawing, trainers, and TM/HM data.
- `index.html`: Game shell and DOM structure.
- `style.css`: Game styling.
- `/tmp/opencode/validate-game.mjs`: Playwright validation script.
- `screenshots/neon-syndicate.jpg`: Existing screenshot to inspect/update.

## Important Context
- Changes are uncommitted; `git status --short` previously showed `.gitignore`, `Agents.md`, `capture.sh`, `game.js`, `index.html`, `start.sh`, `startup.sh`, and `style.css` as untracked.
- When the last Pokémon faints, `battleTurn()` currently ends with `b.result='YOUR CREW IS DOWN — RECOVER AT THE DAYCARE'`; implement the requested blackout/base return instead.
- `renderField()` does not render a map canvas or call `drawMap()`; travel buttons directly assign the destination and call `save();render();`.
- `INITIAL` has `world:{x:360,y:285}` but no step counter.
- `fieldTrainer()` creates one trainer per location with `defeated:false`; `finishBattle()` permanently sets `state.trainers[b.id].defeated=true`.
- `MOVE_ITEMS` derives battle `power` by scaling `sourcePower` (`Math.round(sourcePower/7)`) and assigns each TM only its listed type as eligibility; source-accurate move behavior/data remains to be implemented.
- `KANTO_TOWNS` includes ten destinations.
